I’m a 24-year-man. I go to the gym around four times a week, and I’m currently focused on building muscle and improving my physical fitness. I also spend time working on my online business, which involves selling makeup and skincare products.
I’ve been experiencing sleep disturbances for around 3–4 weeks. I usually fall asleep without difficulty, but I wake up after approximately 4–6 hours, regardless of what time I go to bed.
When I wake up, I still feel sleepy and my eyes feel heavy, but I cannot fall asleep again easily. My body feels relaxed, but I remain awake. I don’t necessarily have racing thoughts or anxiety when this happens, although I sometimes feel frustrated because I cannot get back to sleep.
This happens almost every night and affects my daytime energy and concentration, causing mild to noticeable fatigue.
Before this period, I sometimes woke up during the night, but I could usually fall back asleep quickly. The current problem started without any obvious trigger and began before I started taking Sulpiride.
I also have some emotional difficulties in my romantic relationships, including stress and overthinking at times. However, I’m not sure whether these issues are contributing to my sleep problems, and I don’t want to assume they are the cause.
I don’t experience snoring, choking, palpitations, sweating, or pain that wakes me up. I sometimes feel an internal sensation of warmth in my hands and feet, without tingling or numbness. I’m not sure how long this sensation lasts.
I’d like to understand what might be causing these sleep disturbances and whether my lifestyle, emotional stress, or any physical factors could be contributing to them.
